subject: ai
fixes: f-ai-uninformed-search-properties meaning (DLS): 'it is not optimal even when l >= d' was wrong for l = d with equal step costs (no goal is shallower than d, so any goal found is at the shallowest depth). Changed to 'not optimal in general: with l > d it can return a goal deeper (and costlier) than the shallowest one', with the l = d case stated explicitly.

c-ai-uninformed-search example (DFS): the trace's result depends on an unstated convention. Verified by simulation: with the goal test on pop DFS returns S-A-C-G (cost 10) after expanding S, A, C, as written; with the goal test on generation it returns S-A-G (cost 13) after 2 expansions. Stated the pop convention and added the alternative outcome.

c-ai-a-star-search math: 'Weighted A* expands fewer nodes but only guarantees a cost at most W*C*' changed to 'usually expands fewer nodes, but it is no longer optimal: with an admissible h it only guarantees a cost at most W*C*' (fewer expansions is not guaranteed; the W*C* bound needs admissibility).

f-ai-resolution meaning and c-ai-entailment-inference math (first-order resolution): 'a unifier makes complementary literals identical' corrected to 'a unifier makes the atoms of two literals of opposite sign identical, so that the literals become complementary'.

c-ai-first-order-logic definition: an interpretation was said to fix only the domain, constants and predicate extensions, although the same definition introduces function symbols. Added 'the function on the domain that each function symbol denotes'.

f-ai-bayes-net-factorization latex/meaning: the factorization used \text{parents}(X_i), the parameter count \text{Pa}(X_i), and the meaning \text{Parents}(X_i), while only Pa(X_i) is defined in the variables. Unified on \text{Pa}(X_i) and defined it in the meaning.

c-ai-sampling-inference definition: 'All four are consistent' stated without the condition Gibbs sampling needs. Added that the Gibbs chain must be ergodic, which holds e.g. when every CPT entry is strictly positive (matching the condition already given in the math section and in f-ai-likelihood-weighting-gibbs).

f-ai-likelihood-weighting-gibbs meaning and c-ai-sampling-inference math: the likelihood-weighting weakness was attributed only to evidence position ('when the evidence lies downstream ... most samples get tiny weights'). Restated as in the standard textbook: weights degrade as the number of (or unlikeliness of the) evidence values grows, worse when evidence is late in the topological order, so a few samples dominate the estimate.

c-ai-sampling-inference math: 'A Boolean X ... is set to true iff u < p' was stated as a fact; relabelled as a common convention, with an instruction to use the rule a question states (as the formula card already does).

c-ai-propositional-logic gateRelevance: removed the unsupported frequency claim that tautology MSQs 'are often implications whose premise is a conjunction of literals'; replaced with the verifiable reference to the one official instance (2024 DA paper Q.29, checked in content/pyqs/2024/DA2024-S1-Q29.json).

All 10 concepts' gateRelevance: the lead-in 'Typical question patterns:' implied a frequency that nothing in content/exam/pattern.json supports (several listed patterns, such as IDS node-count NATs, model-counting NATs and 8-puzzle numericals, have no official DA question in content/pyqs). Changed to 'Patterns to prepare for:', the wording used by the other subjects' concept files.

c-ai-heuristics definition: 'a dominating heuristic makes A* expand no more nodes' qualified with 'for consistent heuristics ... (apart from ties at f = C*)', the conditions under which the surely-expanded argument in the same concept's math section holds.

f-ai-prior-rejection-sampling example: '540 kept' is an expectation (N*P(c) = 540), yet the estimate 290/540 used it as an exact count. Labelled 540/460 as expected numbers and made the estimate conditional on exactly 540 being kept.

Verified without change: all 16 formulas' LaTeX, conditions and variable meanings; every worked example in both files recomputed with python3 (search traces simulated, 8-puzzle optimum h* = 14 confirmed by BFS, Knuth-Moore best-case leaf counts confirmed on perfectly ordered random trees, propositional and first-order claims checked by truth-table and finite-domain enumeration including the 343/169 interpretation counts, every Bayesian-network number checked by full-joint enumeration). Cross-links are all valid and reciprocal, every ai subtopic in taxonomy.txt is covered by a concept, the content agrees with the official keys of the 17 ai PYQs in content/pyqs (e.g. |h1 - h2| admissible, non-strict alpha-beta pruning tests, VE exact / sampling approximate), and the validator reports no KaTeX or $-pairing issues.
method: Independent review with python3 recomputation of every worked example
